slides.sub: Payments on account can add half a year's tax on top. Here is how it works.
slides.title: First tax return? Your January bill could be bigger

body: They are payments towards your next tax bill.
Each one is half of the tax you owed last year.
They are due by 31 January and 31 July.
slides.title: What payments on account are

body: Your last bill was less than £1,000.
Or you paid more than 80% of your tax outside Self Assessment, for example through your tax code.
slides.title: When you don't pay them

slides.note: First year in Self Assessment, no payments on account made before, under 80% of tax paid at source. Illustration only.
slides.title: Worked example: first year

body: You can ask HMRC to reduce your payments on account.
If you reduce them too far, you pay interest on the difference.
